newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar jumps vs yen by Tokyo noon on Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Dollar jumps vs yen by Tokyo noon on Sakakibara.

text.p: 0313 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar jumped against the yen in late morning Tokyo on Tuesday in reaction to reported dollar-supportive remarks by senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, dealers said.
His comments prompted a slew of short-covering and set off stop-loss buying, taking the dollar out of its recent narrow range, but exporter sales were expected on the upside.

Sakakibara was quoted by a foreign wire service as saying that the foreign exchange market has excessive expectations of the yen's appreciation, which are not justified, and that Japan and the rest of the Group of Seven (G7) nations have no intention of using foreign exchange rates as a trade tool.
He also reportedly said that Japan's trade surplus will not put upward pressure on the yen.

A city bank dealer said: "The dollar rose in reaction to his comments and stop-loss purchases were triggered near 114.20-30 yen. But I think the dollar will begin to ease gradually in the afternoon as its topside remains heavy on exporter offers."
A rise in dollar/yen late in the morning also encouraged traders to cover mark short positions against the yen in cross trade, pushing the dollar/mark rate down as a result, dealers said.
The mark was quoted around 63.83/86 yen at 0339 GMT, compared with 63.49 yen in late New York trade on Monday.

But dealers said sentiment towards the mark remains bearish, so buying interest on dips will keep the dollar's downside well-supported against the mark. They added, however, that a test of 1.80 marks during Tokyo trading time may be difficult to achieve without fresh trading incentives.
On Monday, the greenback twice charged towards 1.80 marks, but failed to break through the key resistance.
"The market is cautious about possible verbal intervention when the greenback nears 1.80 marks," a dealer at a long-term credit bank said.
The market awaits a news briefing by Sakakibara to be held at 6.30 p.m. (0930 GMT) after his official appointment to the post of vice finance minister for international affairs.
But a city bank dealer said: "We are focusing on the news briefing, but I doubt that he will comment on the forex market because the news briefing is on his new appointment."
The outgoing MOF vice minister for international affairs, Takatoshi Kato, will also attend the news briefing.
Recent turmoil in Southeast Asian currencies has provided support to the yen, which is seen as a safe-haven currency, but dealers said the impact of the recent woes has dissipated somewhat.
"We don't see safe-haven yen buying as much as we did when Thailand decided to float its currency," she said.
The dollar closed at 113.95/05 yen and 1.7950/60 yen in New York on Monday.
--- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8584
